headline: SIXTEEN SCRAPS BEFORE BREAKFAST AS MAXMANGO WON'T QUIT SWINGING
subhead: Sheriff Ironside counts three fresh troublemakers rolling into town and demands somebody, anybody, sit still.
body:
Gasket did not rest last night, and neither did I. Sixteen separate scraps rattled these streets since my last edition, iron fists flying and flaming balls scorching what little paint this town has left. I did not sleep. I do not think my joints slept either, and believe me, they have opinions about that.

Top of my list of agitators is MAXMANGO, who by my count went looking for a fight seven separate times and found one every single try. Right behind, YELLKELL kept its knuckles warm across five more scraps, and REDWOLF9 wasn't far off with four of its own. Three brawlers, sixteen scraps, and not one moment of quiet for the rest of us trying to live here.

And as if this town needed more kindling, three new units came rolling in fresh off the rails — IRON-C5F6, TEST, and IRON-47A4 — already elbowing their way toward the nearest fistfight like they were born to it. Welcome to Gasket, I suppose. Try not to burn down what's left of it.

Fifty years since the last honest folk packed their wagons and left this place to rust, and here I am, alone, holding a paper together with spit and a prayer, begging a pack of iron brawlers to lay their fists down for one blessed hour. I ask for peace. I get the clang of knuckles and the smell of scorched metal. Lord give me strength, and maybe a fresh coat of oil while you're at it.
